items.title: US stocks: US market falls as hot inflation, hawkish Fed fuel rate-hike fears
points: US stocks closed lower after hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthened expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike and raised the possibility of more aggressive tightening.
Rising Treasury yields and weakness in technology stocks, particularly Nvidia, weighed on the market, while investors also assessed hawkish Fed comments and Anthropic’s upcoming IPO.

items.title: Next-Gen Hyundai Creta Spied: Electric Boss Mode, Off-White Cabin, and More Space
points: This might be a hot take, but I strongly believe that the Hyundai Bayon walks so that the next-generation Hyundai Creta can run.
Even before the Bayon was officially unveiled, rumors of a bigger, more spacious, and more muscular Creta were already doing the rounds online.
Hyundai clearly wants to position the Creta as a stronger alternative for Seltos buyers, and that’s perfectly fine.
That’s precisely where the new Bayon fits in, potentially taking over the ₹10 lakh (ex-showroom) price point that the 2027 Creta could leave well behind.
In fact, the new Creta should be based on the new Global K3 platform, which the new Kia Seltos already uses.
However, the 2027 Creta could also debut with a strong hybrid powertrain.

If these images are anything to go by, the Bayon could possibly sport a more tech-loaded cabin than Hyundai’s own top-selling Creta. … The Hyundai Creta has been the benchmark of the mid-size SUV segment in India, and not just for a year or two, but for a…

items.title: Defaults Rattle Brazil’s Shadow Banks, Spark Regulatory Scrutiny
points: Investors keep pouring money into Brazil’s so-called shadow-banking market even as defaults continue to climb.

Total FIDCs under management jumped 14% this year through September, to 978.8 billion reais ($178 billion), and have doubled in the past three years, according to Uqbar, a data and research company that specializes in structured finance and securitization.

“The unemployment rate is expected to rise in 2027, which probably means more defaults on loans and FIDCs,” said Christopher Smith, a credit portfolio manager at Capitania Investimentos SA, which oversees 22 billion reais in assets.
According to KPMG and Brazil’s digital credit association, two-thirds of fintechs surveyed cited FIDCs as their primary source of funding in 2026.
The number of funds grew almost 8% this year this year through September, reaching 4,197, while default rates climbed to 6.17% from 5.95% in September 2025, according to Uqbar data.

items.title: Chile Pension Funds’ Swap Losses Narrow as Treasuries Rally
points: (Bloomberg) -- Chilean pension funds narrowed their market-value losses on foreign interest-rate swaps in October as a rally in US Treasuries provided some relief to a system under heavy pressure from politicians to reduce risks and boost payments.

The AFPs, as the funds are known, had $2.9 billion in mark-to-market losses on foreign interest-rate swaps with international banks at the end of last month, according to figures released Tuesday by the pension regulator.
That was down from $7.7 billion at the end of September.
In October, however, US Treasuries rallied again, with the 10-year yield falling more than 30 basis points from a peak of about 5.3%, its biggest monthly decline since 2023.
Chile’s government had already reported that mark-to-market losses on interest rate swaps fell to about $7 billion as of Oct.
20, down from $10.1 billion at the end of September.
The more conservative D and E funds, which had been hit hardest by the rise in long-term interest rates, rebounded in October rising 1.8% and 3.2%, respectively.

items.title: Fed’s Bowman Warns of Stock Correction If AI Bets Don’t Pan Out
points: Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman said she sees a number of risks to economic activity from financial markets, including a sharp downturn in stock prices if returns on investments in artificial intelligence fall short of expectations.

Speaking in Washington on Tuesday, Bowman flagged the risk of “a large correction in equity valuations” stemming from AI returns, along with “a sharp increase in private longer-term rates.” “Lower equity prices could undermine the resilience in consumer…
“This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2%.” Fed officials left interest rates unchanged at their Oct.
27-28 meeting after raising them by a quarter percentage point in September.
That was the first rate hike since 2023 as policymakers seek to cool inflation that has been above their 2% target for more than five years.

Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
points: The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K.
The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister.
Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought.
The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said.
The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon.
Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said.

items.title: Port of Brunswick Expands Auto Shipping Capacity as Georgia Manufacturing Booms
points: The Georgia Ports Authority is expanding automotive shipping capacity at the Port of Brunswick as a growing number of global automakers establish manufacturing operations across the state, strengthening Georgia’s position as a major hub for vehicle…

At its annual State of the Port of Brunswick event on Tuesday, port officials highlighted new automotive investments, rising demand for roll-on/roll-off (RoRo) shipping and a nearly $5 billion infrastructure investment program planned over the next decade.
The Port of Brunswick, which the authority identifies as a U.S. leader in automotive imports and exports, has experienced 277% growth over the past decade, according to the authority.
A fourth RoRo berth is now 60% complete and scheduled to open in December 2027.

Kia has operated its manufacturing plant in West Point since 2009, while electric vehicle maker Rivian is developing a $5 billion manufacturing facility at Stanton Springs North, expected to create 7,500 long-term jobs by 2030.

items.title: Dangote Refinery Gets $4.1 Billion Orders in Top Africa IPO
points: (Bloomberg) -- Africa’s biggest refinery attracted about 5.85 trillion naira ($4.1 billion) of applications for shares in the continent’s largest public offering to date, almost three times the amount it sought to raise, according to people familiar with…

The Public Investment Corp., which oversees about $220 billion in pensions of South African state workers and is the continent’s biggest money manager, asked for a large allocation the people said, declining to specify the amount.
Nigerian pension managers covering about 11 million members also asked for allocations, they said.
Investors have raced to secure a stake in the Lagos-based crude-processing facility that’s Africa’s largest as well as one of the biggest globally and owned by its richest man, Aliko Dangote.
Exchanges across the continent are providing structures to give buyers access to the listing that has attracted applications from all 54 countries in the region.
Trading will start 15 business days after the allotment date, according to the prospectus, which will likely be on Dec.

items.title: MSM: Shipmanagement’s next advantage will be trust not size
points: Consolidation is reshaping shipmanagement, but Faouzi Fradi, chief executive of MSM, does not believe getting bigger has to mean becoming more distant from owners, vessels or seafarers.

MSM, formerly known as Maryam Shipmanagement, recently rebranded as part of a broader shift from a predominantly group-focused shipmanager towards an international third-party management platform, while also moving into new headquarters in Dubai.
“The rebrand is only the starting point.
Dubai will remain its centre, while the company strengthens its reach through Turkey, Greece, Norway, India and the Philippines.

We want controlled growth, closer access to clients, and owners who value transparency, direct access to decision-makers and a manager prepared to think like an owner.” MSM is positioning itself as an owner-aligned alternative to the largest global…
For Fradi, there is no target fleet size that defines success.
Its team also has experience with containerships and offshore vessels.

items.title: Vaiko releases 34-year crime report; rebukes allies for criticising T.N. government
points: Vaiko interacting with journalists in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: RAGHUNATHAN SR Amid ongoing accusations by Opposition parties of increase in crime and deteriorating law and order in Tamil Nadu, MDMK general secretary Vaiko on Tuesday released a…
Addressing journalists in Chennai on Tuesday, he said except the IUML and the MDMK, the other parties within the ruling alliance have been criticising the administration.
Mr. Vaiko released a list detailing crimes committed in the State between May 1991 and May 2026.
In particular, he detailed the circumstances surrounding his arrest under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) in July 2002.

He noted that upon learning of the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to detain him under POTA, he advanced his return from the United States — originally scheduled for July 15 — and arrived in Chennai on July 11 to court arrest.

items.title: ‘Nonsense Rate’: Iran War Exposes Turmoil Behind Key Tanker Benchmark
points: By Jack Farchy and Alex Longley (Bloomberg) — In March this year, inside a 282-year-old institution responsible for one of the most important prices in global oil markets, one man staged a quiet protest.
“Nonsense rate,” Christopher Loveday wrote on March 23 in an internal document at the Baltic Exchange, where he was responsible for helping produce the world’s benchmark rate for shipping oil.
It has shown that numerous people involved in the key oil tanker rate, called TD3C, expressed reservations as the Baltic Exchange continued to publish the price in the early weeks of the war.

Mercuria, whose demands have changed several times since it launched the case in April, is seeking to have the judge declare that the Baltic was wrong to keep publishing the TD3C index in the initial phase of the war from March to July.

items.title: U.S. Closes First Oil and Gas Production Loan Under Revamped Energy Financing Program
points: An oil and gas drilling platform stands offshore in the Gulf of Mexico in Dauphin Island, Alabama, U.S. , October 5, 2013.

REUTERS/Steve Nesius/File Photo The U.S. Department of Energy has closed a $480 million loan to modernize 22 offshore platforms in the Gulf of Mexico, marking the department’s first completed loan financing domestic oil and natural gas production.
The financing, announced Tuesday, will support Arena Energy’s Project Elkhorn, a major infrastructure redevelopment effort in the Southern Eugene Island area off Louisiana.

The loan comes through the Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), formerly known as the Loan Programs Office, which the Trump administration has redirected toward expanding domestic energy production and strengthening existing…
The Energy Department said the financing was made possible by provisions in President Donald Trump’s Working Families Tax Cut legislation.

“The United States is the world’s largest producer and exporter of oil and natural gas, and thanks to President Trump, American energy production will continue to grow,” Energy Secretary Chris Wright said.

items.title: Wall St retreats as hot inflation data, Fed comments fuel rate worries
points: The Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4% last month, its third straight gain of 0.4% or more and above the 0.3% estimate of economists polled by Reuters, after advancing 0.6% in September.

The data came after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise short-term borrowing costs in December even if data shows inflation cooled last month, and should consider an upsized half-point rate hike if the inflation picture worsens.
Markets are now completely pricing in a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed's December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from 84% on Monday.

The two-year US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, surged 19.1 basis points to 4.738% and was on track for its biggest daily gain since April 9, 2025, after US President Donald Trump launched his…

items.title: IT hubs see 82% commute by personal vehicles, just 2% use public transport
points: Anand along with senior officials unveiled the logo of ‘Cyberabad Moves’, a three-day exhibition and symposium scheduled to be held from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub, Hyderabad.

As Cyberabad grapples with growing traffic congestion, an overwhelming 82% of commuter movement across its key IT hubs is accounted for by personal vehicles, while public transport contributes just around 2%, highlighting the region’s dependence on private…
According to data presented by Cyberabad Police and the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), traffic across 15 key IT-sector locations exceeds 2.5 million vehicles and people every day.

The figures underline the scale of the mobility challenge in one of Hyderabad’s fastest-growing employment hubs, which has a resident population of around 3.5 million spread across approximately 637 sq. km, apart from a substantial daily commuter…

With around six lakh IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) employees represented by the corporates participating in a stakeholder interaction on Tuesday, Cyberabad Police are looking to bring companies on board to encourage a shift towards shared and…

items.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
points: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C.
Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity.
Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”.
There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations.

The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August.
In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning.
Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights.

items.title: Corn Soars After USDA Cuts American Yield in Another Surprise
points: (Bloomberg) -- Corn surged the most in three months after the US Department of Agriculture surprised traders with a bigger-than-expected cut to yield and production of America’s most widely grown crop.

While a small trim in USDA’s monthly supply and demand outlook was anticipated, the scale of the reduction caught traders off guard, with futures in Chicago rising by as much as 3.7% after the report was published.
The USDA pared back yields in key corn-growing states including Illinois, Indiana and Nebraska, estimating national production at 15.893 billion bushels.
USDA lifted its soybean production estimate to a fresh record high of 4.57 billion bushels.
President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are expected to meet later in November.

The American Soybean Association said that while it was “pleased” by the purchase commitments, the existing 10% tariff gives an added advantage to South American imports in China, according to a Tuesday letter from the group.

items.title: World Wars and India’s sacrifice
points: Indian troops on the Eritrean front during World War II. | Photo Credit: The Hindu Photo Archives On the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, most Commonwealth and other allied nations fall silent for two minutes to honour the fallen of the two…
India has an uneasy relationship with Remembrance Day.
However, the idea that the World Wars were something that happened to someone else, somewhere else, could not be further from the truth.
Indian ambivalence over the two World Wars belies its enormous contribution to fighting fascism.
Undivided (British) India sent 1.5 million men to fight in World War I, 74,000 of whom never returned home.
For WWII, India produced the largest volunteer army of 2.5 million soldiers, with 87,00–89,000 making the ultimate sacrifice.
Whereas the Indians who fought in the Great War were mostly sent to distant lands, in WWII, about 7,00,000 of them were defending Indian territory.
The war came home to India when Japan invaded the country in March 1944.

items.title: Civil police officer injured in attack by detained man in Keralam’s Kochi
points: A civil police officer (CPO) attached to the Ernakulam North police station was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance near the North overbridge bit on his hands when he was being taken in a police vehicle for…
This comes two days after another CPO who was on traffic duty at the High Court bus stand was injured after a recklessly driven private bus rammed him.
The incident occurred after the officer stopped a row of vehicles for an ambulance to pass through.

The Ernakulam Central police have registered a case against Muhammed Iqbal, 25, of Sashthamkotta in Kollam who, while being reportedly under the influence of intoxicants, bit on the hands of the police officer named Ajith Paul.
He was seated on the last row of the police vehicle, from where he jumped into the middle row seat and reportedly tried to force open the door as the vehicle reached the Ernakulam General Hospital.

items.title: Gem Granites Veeramani’s daughter Archana moves Madras High Court alleging human rights violations by SIT
points: The petitioner claimed no summons, warrant, court order, Look Out Circular or any such document was provided to her. | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Archana Veeramani, 49, the daughter of R.
Lakshminarayanan is expected to hear her plea on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
The High Court Registry had numbered her writ petition (criminal) subject to maintainability.

In her affidavit, Ms. Veeramani said, her father had been arrayed as the prime accused in a case booked by the police under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act of 2012 and other laws.
She was not an accused in that case at least as on October 23, 2026 and no court had restrained her from undertaking foreign travel.
Therefore, she had booked a flight from Chennai to Singapore on that day to visit her son and help him take medical treatment for his ailments.
After she had boarded the plane at around 2 p.m. on October 23, the airline staff forcefully deboarded her without assigning any reason, the petitioner alleged.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 3% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
points: Nov 10 (Reuters) - Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year.
Spot gold was down 2.7% at $4,028.39 per ounce by 1:53 p.m.
US gold futures for December delivery settled 2.0% lower at $4,030.20 per ounce.
The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise.

Bets on a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December started to build after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support more aggressive action in the event of a too-hot Consumer Price Index report.
The probability of a 25 bp hike is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to 10% from 0% before the data, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

items.title: How to Turn Any GIF Into an Animated WhatsApp Sticker in 10 Seconds on Android and iPhone
points: WhatsApp lets you turn GIFs into animated stickers and share them directly in your chats.
You can use your phone’s keyboard, WhatsApp’s built-in sticker editor, or a third-party tool to create stickers from GIFs you already have.
Here’s how to do it on Android and iPhone.
Android users have a couple of ways to convert GIFs into WhatsApp stickers.
If you don’t have Gboard installed, you can use WhatsApp’s own sticker editor. iPhone users can convert a GIF into a sticker directly from a WhatsApp chat.
Tap Edit Sticker, make your changes, and tap Send.

items.title: Apple Starts Selling $49.99 AI Usage Packs for Creator Studio Subscribers
points: Apple has started selling paid usage top-ups for select AI features in Apple Creator Studio.
The only available option is a one-time $49.99 (approx. ₹4,500) intelligence usage pack.
Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the US, with discounted education pricing also available.
Logic Pro is currently the only Creator Studio app offering the paid top-ups.
Apple is expected to extend the option to Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro and the iWork apps, including Pages, Keynote and Numbers, as their previously announced updates arrive this month.
Apple has yet to disclose how many additional generations or tokens a $49.99 pack includes.
NPCI’s UPI and Services Steering Committee decided on October 13, 2026, to defer the rollout of the new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) until after Diwali, citing the festive season.

With Diwali falling on November 8 this year, the revised implementation window has arrived, although … Alongside the M6 iMac and M6 MacBook Pro, Apple has also rolled out a major Creator Studio upgrade.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Series Camera Specs Leak
points: SammyGuru has revealed the camera sensors Samsung is reportedly evaluating for the Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro and S27 Ultra.
Both phones are reportedly being tested with a 50MP main camera using either the Sony IMX955 or Samsung S5KGNG, the latter being the same sensor used in the Galaxy S26 and S26+.
The ultrawide camera could retain the 12MP Sony IMX564, which Samsung has used since the Galaxy S23.
Both are reportedly being tested with a 200MP Samsung S5KHP6 main sensor.
The two phones are also expected to share a 50MP ultrawide camera, using either the Samsung S5KJN3 or Sony IMX855, alongside a 16MP Samsung S5K2P5 selfie camera.
The S27 Pro is reportedly getting a 3X Samsung S5K3LD sensor, the same unit used for the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 3X zoom camera.
That is smaller than the 1/1.95-inch telephoto sensor on the Pixel 11 Pro and considerably smaller than the 1/1.56-inch 200MP telephoto sensors used across the OPPO Find X10 series.

items.title: Focus on Tamil during Kandasashthi: Minister
points: Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S.
Ramesh on Tuesday said that Tamil language and literature will be given priority during the Kandasashthi festival in all major Murugan temples.
He urged temples under the purview of the department to ensure that Odhuvars chant/sing the Thirupugazh, Thirumurai, and Kandasashthi kavacham.
Priests should also give priority to Tamil in all pujas and proceedings during the festival.
Discourses and concerts should be in Tamil as well, he added.

In a set of directions issued to executive officers of temples, the Minister said that special arrangements must be made for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and mothers-to-be at temples for darshan.

Mr. Ramesh said that temple officials should coordinate with the police, fire and other departments to ensure proper arrangements such as drinking water, toilets and medical care for devotees for darshan, during Kandasashthi and Sura Samharam.

items.title: "Blatantly Political": India Rejects US Body's Remarks On Gurdwara Attacks
points: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) is a "biased" entity with a "blatantly" political agenda, New Delhi said on Tuesday, trashing remarks by two senior officials of the organisation claiming that Sikh gurdwaras have been targeted…

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also wondered why the USCIRF chose to remain silent on attacks on religious places in the US and on racial abuse targeting the Indian community in that country.
Last week, two senior officials of the USCIRF, flagging concerns over "attacks" on gurdwaras in India, urged the US government to press New Delhi to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable.
"The USCIRF is a biased and ill-informed organisation with a blatantly political agenda," Jaiswal said, responding to a question on the comments by the USCIRF officials.

"It is particularly telling that the USCIRF and its commissioners have consistently chosen to remain silent on attacks on religious places in the US and on the hate crimes and racial abuse targeted at the Indian community in the US.

items.title: US stocks: Five things to know about Anthropic
points: Founded by former OpenAI researchers, Anthropic has grown into a major AI company backed by Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Nvidia.
As the Claude developer prepares for a landmark IPO, its safety-focused philosophy, unconventional roots and clash with the Pentagon are drawing renewed scrutiny.

items.title: Central Pollution Body Explains Data Gaps On Diwali Night
points: The past couple of days have triggered immense conversation and scrutiny around AQI numbers.

On Diwali, while the Central Pollution Control Board's (CPCB) Sameer app showed numbers pegged around 400 in the 'severe' category, websites and private applications showed AQI numbers even above 1000.
As soon as the numbers came in, netizens compared the figures and criticised government numbers for being opaque in their reporting of AQI.
The CPCB has now broken its silence and issued a clarification on the core mechanics of India's National Air Quality Index (NAQI) framework, its design methodology, and its international alignment.
The body says, "The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a tool for effective communication of air quality status to people in terms that are easy to understand.
The CPCB clarifies that this ceiling is an intentional design choice modelled after global standards: "The upper limit of 500 represents the highest level of health concern.

items.title: 'List Measures To Stop Digital Arrests, Cybercrimes': Top Court To WhatsApp
points: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it of their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country.
The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on November 23.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken.

"WhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes.
They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C," the bench said in its order.

Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, the bench had said the proposed RBI regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive…

items.title: Periyar Library Book Scam: High Court Orders Police Case, Freezes Publisher's Bank Account
points: A police case should be lodged immediately into the alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for public libraries in Tamil Nadu, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court told the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption on Tuesday.
The court has also ordered the freezing of bank accounts belonging to Agal Vilakku Publications, its proprietor Mohan and others involved in the alleged scam.
The Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi directed the government to initiate disciplinary action, including suspension of officials involved.
The Director of Public Libraries has been asked to identify officials responsible for fraudulent procurements over the past two years.
The contempt case stems from an order from June 2024 which directed the government to follow the Transparent Book Procurement Policy.
The latest order also invokes Rule 18(4) of the Tamil Nadu Public Libraries Rules, 1950, which requires books to have general interest and cultural value and bars works of doubtful taste.

items.title: UP Teen Girl Calls Helpline, Stops Her Own Child Marriage
points: A 16-year-old girl from eastern Uttar Pradesh picked up the phone and made the most important call of her life, defying her parents, who had decided for her a life far away in Saudi Arabia with a 25-year-old man.
Instead of checking her bridal wear for her marriage scheduled for Wednesday, she dialled 1098 -- the child helpline -- to set in motion a process that eventually stopped her child marriage.
The teenager, Gudiya (name changed), took the step last week after learning that her family had arranged her marriage in a village in Bairia area of Ballia district in UP.

"This girl was remarkably aware that she was below the legal age for marriage, which is 18 years, and thus contacted the helpline before the scheduled wedding," District Probation Officer Amarendra Kumar Potsayan told PTI on the phone.

items.title: India's Oldest Industry Body FICCI Warns Air Pollution Costs $95 Billion Annually
points: In its report, 'Clean Air, Healthy India', FICCI argues that the country can no longer treat air pollution as merely an environmental issue and must instead place it at the heart of India's healthcare agenda.
The Air Quality Index is breaking records, and out of the 100 most polluted cities of the world, 99 are from India.
More than two million deaths in India in 2023 were attributable to air pollution.
Rarely does FICCI, which represents more than 2.5 lakh companies across India, issue such alarming assessments.
It notes that approximately 1.3 billion working days are lost annually and productivity can decline by 8 per cent to 10 per cent during heavily polluted periods.
The 76-page report prepared in partnership with EY highlights that air pollution-related losses could be as high as $95 billion a year or a loss of about 3 per cent of GDP annually.

items.title: On Camera, Gunmen Chase Man, Daughter, Open Fire In Punjab's Fazilka
points: CCTV footage of a brazen firing incident in Punjab's Fazilka has sent shockwaves through the area after unidentified armed men chased a man returning home with his young daughter and opened fire at his car in broad daylight.
The incident took place in Sureshwala village near Fazilka, where the attackers allegedly followed the victim all the way to his residence before firing two rounds at his vehicle.
The father and daughter had a narrow escape, while bullets struck the windshield and body of the car.
The CCTV footage of the incident, which has surfaced on social media, shows the shocking sequence of events and has triggered fear among local residents.
According to the victim, Manish Kumar, he was returning from Fazilka city with his young daughter when a Swift car started following him.
Manish alleged that as soon as he stopped his car outside his house, occupants of the Swift got out and opened fire at his vehicle.
